text: Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 1,820 patients treated at the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University from 1 January 2020 to 1 January 2026; 453 met the definite AMI definition. Core-7 combined neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte, platelet, mean platelet volume, red cell distribution width, and hemoglobin using elastic-net logistic regression. Performance was assessed by repeated five-fold cross-validation with preprocessing and tuning restricted to training data. PIV was the principal comparator, the Enhanced model added fibrinogen, and a temporal sensitivity analysis used institutionally deidentified dates shifted by no more than six months.

This was a single-center retrospective observational study conducted in the Department of Cardiology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University, Urumqi, Xinjiang, China, using records from Coronary Heart Disease Unit I. The study period was 1 January 2020 to 1 January 2026, and the source population comprised patients who underwent coronary angiography during this period. In accordance with institutional data-privacy requirements, exact calendar dates were deidentified before clinical records were released for research. Each patient's dates were shifted by a randomized value within +/-182 days, while intervals between events for the same patient were preserved. These shifted dates were used only for a temporal sensitivity analysis and were not interpreted as the actual recruitment calendar. Because a uniform prospective index time could not be reconstructed for all patients, the present study focused on retrospective AMI phenotype discrimination rather than future-event prediction.

Primary internal validation used stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. For each validation fold, predictions were generated from a model fitted without those patients. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals; Brier score, calibration intercept, and calibration slope were used to assess overall performance and calibration [20-26]. Differences in AUC between models were estimated from 1,000 paired patient-level bootstrap resamples of the cross-validated predictions [23,24]. No univariable P-value screening or stepwise variable selection was used. A reference coefficient specification is provided in the supplementary material for reproducibility; the primary performance estimates reflect repeated internal cross-validation rather than a single bedside equation. For the descriptive comparisons in Table 1, continuous variables were compared between the AMI and non-AMI CAD groups using the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using Pearson's chi-square test (with Fisher's exact test reserved for sparse expected cell counts). These Table 1 P values were descriptive only and were not used for predictor selection or model development.

Continuous variables are presented as median [interquartile range] unless otherwise stated. P-values compare definite AMI with definite non-AMI CAD and were calculated using the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables and Pearson's chi-square test for categorical variables; they are descriptive and were not used for model development. Several features strengthen the analysis, including predefined diagnostic mapping, preprocessing restricted to the training data during cross-validation, common cross-validated predictions for model comparisons, assessment of predictor stability, and a conservative temporal sensitivity analysis. The study also has important limitations. It is retrospective and single-center; AMI status was based primarily on discharge diagnoses rather than independent adjudication with serial biomarkers, electrocardiography, imaging, and full clinical context; and no independent external cohort was available. Exact clinical index times could not be standardized for all patients because research dates were deidentified, and fibrinogen measurements were less complete than CBC measurements. Analyzer and platform details were not included in the deidentified research database but can be retrieved from institutional laboratory records if required. These limitations define the next step: independent evaluation with a predefined clinical index time, harmonized laboratory measurements, adjudicated AMI status, and prospective assessment of calibration and clinical utility [20,21,26-30].
